title: Site Sets

hints.text: A site set is how a system extension ships TypoScript. It is a directory Configuration/Sets/<SetName>/ whose config.yaml carries a composer-style name ("typo3/fluid-styled-content"), an optional label, and an optional dependencies list naming other sets by that same name.
Next to config.yaml the set may hold setup.typoscript, settings.definitions.yaml, settings.yaml, labels.xlf, page.tsconfig and route-enhancers.yaml. Only config.yaml is required.

settings.definitions.yaml is where a set declares its settings: a categories map and a settings map, each entry with default, type and category. It is the replacement for TypoScript constants — reaching for constants.typoscript in new code is the mistake to avoid here.
The set's labels.xlf resolves to the translation domain <ext>.sets.<setname>; typo3_translation_domain_lookup computes it from the path.

A page layout the set ships in page.tsconfig declares its columns under mod.web_layout.BackendLayouts, and every column needs an explicit `identifier`: that identifier is what the frontend template addresses as {content.<identifier>}. Leaving it out is accepted on the branches that still fall back to a generated one, and the template can then no longer reach its own content — the page renders empty and nothing is logged.

hints: ExtensionManagementUtility::addTypoScriptSetup() and addStaticFile() are the predecessor and are still called from a few sysexts, addTypoScriptSetup with an includeInSiteSets flag that folds the content into the set mechanism. Both mechanisms coexist; new code ships a set.

hints.text: Site set resolution is covered by functional tests under typo3/sysext/core/Tests/Functional/Site/Set/; the labels have their own check, checkIntegritySetLabels.

title: Page and User TSconfig
hints: TSconfig here means TYPO3 page and user TSconfig, not the tsconfig.json of the TypeScript build. The two are unrelated and neither is a place to configure the other.
A system extension ships defaults in Configuration/page.tsconfig and Configuration/user.tsconfig. Both are auto-loaded from that path — there is nothing to register in ext_localconf.php.
An option is read from the merged page TSconfig. In FormEngine that merge is done by the PageTsConfigMerged data provider, so a provider that reads the option has to depend on it.
A new TSconfig option is user-facing configuration: it needs a Feature changelog entry and documentation, not just the default.
Behaviour that depends on TSconfig is covered by functional tests; the parser itself lives in typo3/sysext/core/Classes/TypoScript/.
